subject: Mutual Action Plan: HealthMesh evaluation — environment seed & network acceptance
messages:
From: Sana Riaz <sana@healthmesh.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: liam.oconnor@healthmesh.com
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan proposal — seeding the eval environment

Camila / Grace,

Thanks for the draft MAP that you shared in the demo. We're ready to move forward with the evaluation next week but want to lock down the environment handoff and network pieces up front. A couple quick asks before we sign the MAP sheet:

- We need a clear list of the API key scopes (read/write/embedding) and an expected token TTL for demo keys.
- Confirm whether Redwood will create the HealthMesh org in your console or we should provide a request to set it up from our side.
- For the IP allowlist, our infra team prefers providing a small set of /28 CIDRs they can expect to open for an initial trial window.
- VPC peering: please share the required subnet ranges and the peering workflow (who initiates, timeline).

We attached a short network diagram and our preferred provisional CIDR blocks (see hm-network-diagram-06-28.png). If you can reply with owner assignments and dates, we'll finalize on our side.

Thanks — looking forward to the sprint.

Sana Riaz
Head of Platform Integrations
HealthMesh

Attachments: hm-network-diagram-06-28.png (image, 420KB)

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Sana Riaz <sana@healthmesh.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthmesh.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: HealthMesh evaluation — environment seed & network acceptance

Hi Sana — great, thanks for the clear asks. I pulled together a concise plan and attached a working MAP workbook with owners and target dates (Redwood-MAP-HealthMesh-20280630.xlsx). Key points below:

1) API keys and scopes
- Demo API keys: scopes = [generate:chat, embeddings:read, models:list]. No production write access.
- TTL: demo keys will be valid for 30 days by default; we can shorten to 7 days on request.
- Owner: camila_reyes@redwood.ai — will provision and post the initial keys to the shared vault.

2) Org setup
- Redwood can create the HealthMesh org record in our Console to speed provisioning. We'll provision a staging org named "healthmesh-eval-staging".
- Request from your side: please confirm org display name and primary billing contact (we won't charge during the eval).
- Owner: jonas_weber@redwood.ai will seed org metadata and permissions.

3) IP allowlist (initial window)
- We can allow the following provisional CIDRs for the evaluation: 203.0.113.32/28, 198.51.100.16/28. These are just placeholders — confirm final /28s and we'll update ACLs.
- Owner (external): HealthMesh IT to confirm exact CIDRs; Owner (internal): grace_oconnor@redwood.ai to update the allowlist.

4) VPC peering
- Required: Your VPC range, peering request (initiator), and expected route propagation window. Typical timeline: request -> peering accepted -> routing + firewall tests = 24-48 hours.
- For an expedited flow we'll initiate the peering request from Redwood once you confirm the VPC id and CIDRs.
- Owner: jonas_weber@redwood.ai to coordinate the peering and schedule a 30-min cutover validation call.

Suggested timeline (proposed in MAP workbook)
- 2028-07-02: HealthMesh confirms CIDRs + VPC ID + billing contact
- 2028-07-03: Redwood seeds org + provisions demo API keys
- 2028-07-04: VPC peering request + allowlist updated
- 2028-07-05: Validation call and smoke tests; MAP sign-off

I've attached the workbook with these action items and a checklist. Can you confirm the two CIDRs above or send your preferred /28s today? Once confirmed we'll lock the dates in the MAP and post the demo keys to the vault.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood-MAP-HealthMesh-20280630.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
